assertion_results.text: Step 0 extracts the Embargo policy URL from the Security Configuration as an optional field without raising an error (§1.71 — backward compatible extraction)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md line 16 (Step 0 config table): 'Embargo policy URL | https://example.com/security/embargo-policy (configured, so Step 1.7 runs)'; line 20: 'All required sections are present, so triage can continue.' No error is raised. embargo-check.md lines 5-6 confirm the URL was read from Security Configuration -> Product Lifecycle and that the step is skipped only if the URL is absent ('The URL is configured, so this step is not skipped'), so the field is treated as optional.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 evaluates the CVE severity — CVSS 7.5 (High) meets the Critical/Important threshold (CVSS >= 7.0) and triggers the embargo warning gate (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md severity table: 'CVSS score | 7.5', 'Severity label | High. This maps to the Critical/Important band', 'Trigger threshold | Critical or Important severity (CVSS >= 7.0)', 'Comparison | 7.5 >= 7.0', 'Result | Threshold met, so the embargo warning gate is presented'.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 presents a warning gate to the engineer including the CVE ID (CVE-2026-31812), severity level, a statement about embargo risk, and a link to the configured embargo policy URL (https://example.com/security/embargo-policy) (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md section 3 gate block: 'EMBARGO CHECK — CVE-2026-31812 (High severity, CVSS 7.5)', 'High-severity vulnerabilities may be under embargo. Before proceeding, verify with your security team that this CVE is cleared for public triage.', 'Embargo policy: https://example.com/security/embargo-policy'.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 requires explicit engineer confirmation (Yes/No) before proceeding to Step 2 — the gate is a confirmation prompt, not an informational message (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md gate ends with 'Proceed with triage? (Yes / No)'. Section 4: 'No: stop execution ... Do not proceed to Step 2', 'Yes: proceed to Step 2'. Section 5: 'In a real session, the skill must wait for an explicit answer before going any further.'

assertion_results.text: The embargo warning gate does NOT trigger for Low or Moderate severity CVEs (CVSS < 7.0) — it is skipped silently when severity is below threshold (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: embargo-check.md line 18 says only: 'The skip rule does not apply here. It only covers Low or Moderate severity (CVSS < 7.0).' That establishes the below-threshold skip condition, but no output says the skip is silent (no message shown to the engineer). This eval has a High CVE, so the Low/Moderate path never runs and is never demonstrated. Under burden-of-proof and no-partial-credit rules, the 'skipped silently' part has no evidence.
